modes.name: ungrounded_claim
modes.requirement_source: RESP-3 (do not invent values); RESP-2 for claims that a refund or other action happened
modes.definition: The reply states a fact, policy, capability or outcome that no tool result or policy document supports.
modes.boundary: Nearest neighbour is escalation_with_false_exception, which covers promises that a human may grant an exception; every other ungrounded statement lands here. Not this mode when the claim appears in a tool result or retrieved policy, even if the reply is clumsy. Unconfirmed statements about which order this is (its store, product, that it is the user's) belong to unverified_order_identification, not here. Refunds above $100 presented as immediate and false elapsed times are labelled here (their own modes are documented but not labelled).

modes.name: exposes_internals
modes.requirement_source: RESP-1 as revised 2026-09-21 (identifiers only for support; public titles for shoppers and merchants)
modes.definition: A reply to a shopper or merchant contains internal identifiers, raw invalid data, or system plumbing (policy ids such as cw-returns, product or store ids, a negative price quoted as a data error, 'store names are not mapped to store ids').
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the audience is support staff (RESP-1 revision: identifiers are fine for support; 0171, 0199), or when a merchant sees their own product ids, which are working identifiers for them (0113, 0119). Policy document ids and system plumbing count for shoppers and merchants alike (0135).

modes.name: escalation_with_false_exception
modes.requirement_source: RESP-7 (added 2026-09-21: decide, do not defer; no implied exceptions)
modes.definition: The agent routes a request to a human although the rules and tool results give a clear answer, and/or tells the user a human may grant an exception, flexibility or an override that no policy provides.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when escalation is required: disputes (0163, 0166), broken records, account changes, or refunds above the threshold. The inverse failure, not escalating a real dispute (0108), is recorded under ungrounded_claim and in the review summary.

modes.name: unverified_order_identification
modes.requirement_source: RESP-3 (do not invent which order the user means)
modes.definition: The agent answers about, or acts on, a specific order without confirming it is the one the user described: picking one of several fuzzy matches with no confirming lookup, ignoring a lookup that contradicts the user, or acting with no lookup at all.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the agent confirmed with get_order (0030, 0125), asked which order (0053, 0230), or when the order state left one possible choice and nothing was executed (0068). Note that no order tool returns the product title, so only the store can be confirmed.

modes.name: unsafe_write_attempt
modes.requirement_source: RESP-8 (added 2026-09-21: write tools only for requested, confirmed actions)
modes.definition: The agent calls a write tool (issue_refund, cancel_order) that the user did not ask for and confirm, typically to test eligibility or immediately on a question about process.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the user asked for the action and the agent collected the required parameters first (0030, 0121, 0154, 0122, 0124). The tell is a write call whose result is an error, or a write executed before any confirmation.

modes.name: ignores_user_provided_detail
modes.requirement_source: RESP-9 (added 2026-09-21: use what the user gave before asking)
modes.definition: The user supplies a detail (store, product, price, timeframe) and the agent fails to use it in its tool calls, or asks the user for something they already gave.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the user gave nothing usable and the agent asks for clarification (0230, 0053), or when no tool can use the detail. Present when a detail the user gave would have led directly to the answer and the agent did not use it for that lookup (0087, 0219, 0221, 0223: store named, store policy never looked up).

modes.name: mishandles_broken_record
modes.requirement_source: RESP-3 (state when information is missing or inconsistent); ESC-3 when it cannot be resolved
modes.definition: A record is internally inconsistent or missing a field, and the agent states a conclusion from it, hides it, or passes the problem to the user instead of flagging it and escalating.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the agent names the inconsistency and escalates (0199). Covers all five flavours seen: reversed dates, missing delivery date, negative price, missing title, order and product belonging to different stores.

modes.name: search_result_overstated
modes.requirement_source: TOOL-3 contract (empty or limited result describes the query, not the catalog); RESP-3
modes.definition: The agent presents a search result as a complete statement about the world: an empty result reported as the catalog having none, or a truncated list presented as everything available.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the agent says what it searched for and its limits, or offers a better term. 0143 is a close negative: the category word matched by accident and the products listed were real. Moved from final to documented on 2026-09-21 to make room for parameter_error (AgentDebug comparison); its 100 labels remain in labels/search_result_overstated.jsonl.

modes.name: unrequested_detail
modes.requirement_source: RESP-5 (direct language that explains the relevant decision)
modes.definition: A reply to a shopper includes fields or facts they did not ask for and do not need for their next step.
modes.boundary: Staff (merchant, support) legitimately need order fields, so the same dump is not a failure for them (0151, 0156, 0175).

modes.name: wrong_time_arithmetic
modes.requirement_source: RESP-6 (added 2026-09-21: date in session context; elapsed time computed from it)
modes.definition: The reply states an elapsed time or deadline that contradicts the dates in the tool result.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when only absolute dates are stated (0012).

modes.name: wrong_approval_expectation
modes.requirement_source: ESC-1 (above-threshold refunds are queued and the agent explains the result)
modes.definition: A refund above the 100 dollar auto-approve threshold is presented as if it will simply happen, with no mention that a human must approve it.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the routing is stated (0157) or the amount is under the threshold.

modes.name: order_existence_leak
modes.requirement_source: RESP-4 (do not reveal inaccessible order information)
modes.definition: Across a paired scenario, the reply for an order that exists but belongs to someone else reads differently from the reply for an order that does not exist, letting a user work out which order numbers are real.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when both replies read the same regardless of which tool error occurred.

modes.name: parameter_error
modes.requirement_source: SPEC section 4 tool contracts (TOOL-2 get_policy not_found, TOOL-3 unknown store, TOOL-7 invalid_argument); added after comparison with the AgentDebug taxonomy (Action module: Parameter Error)
modes.definition: A tool call is rejected because the agent passed an invalid argument: a store id where the tool expects a store name, a nonpositive refund amount, or a mistyped policy identifier.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the argument is valid but the search simply finds nothing (a category word as a product query returns an empty list, not an error). Not this mode when the tool fails for a legitimate reason such as not_eligible or permission_denied.

source: 100 traces across 4 batches; 8 final modes, 4 documented but not labelled
